generator: tools/import/constellations.mjs (rerun it to rebuild every file here; the pins below are checked by SHA-256)

figures.what: IAU constellation stick figures (drawn for the IAU by Sky & Telescope, Alan MacRobert; Roger Sinnott and Rick Fienberg), as Hipparcos-number lists typed in by the Stellarium team

boundaries.what: IAU constellation boundaries: the corner points of Delporte (1930), epoch B1875, as published in the same Stellarium file
boundaries.from: Stellarium skycultures/modern_iau/index.json at commit dc5679c9723685585196c4d6ecd7ffd33da59ecd (edges, edges_source https://pbarbier.com/constellations/edges_18.txt)
boundaries.reference: Delporte, E. 1930, Delimitation scientifique des constellations (Cambridge University Press); Davenhall and Leggett 1989, CDS catalogue VI/49

names.what: IAU constellation names, abbreviations, English names and genitives
names.from: IAU constellations page, Internet Archive copy of 2025-01-08 (the page is no longer on iau.org)

crossCheck.what: CDS VI/49 bound_20.dat (Davenhall and Leggett 1989), used only to check the J2000 boundaries; none of it is shipped

changes: Figures: each polyline split into steps; 4 zero-length and 87 repeated steps dropped; ends kept as Hipparcos numbers where the engine's star list holds the star, otherwise given as a J2000 position.

Boundaries: edges chained into one closed outline per constellation (Serpens has two); points added every 1 degree of arc or less along each edge (meridian edges at constant right ascension, parallel edges at constant declination, as Delporte drew them); every point precessed from B1875.0 to J2000 with the IAU 1976 precession angles; stored to 3 decimals as flat right ascension, declination pairs in degrees. The last point joins the first; it is not repeated.
Names: the four columns of the IAU table kept as published (the pronunciation text dropped).

crossCheck.method: Every VI/49 J2000 point (original and interpolated) is compared with our outline of the same code drawn at 0.05 degree spacing (distance to the nearest great-circle segment); every original VI/49 corner is compared with the nearest corner of ours. In the other direction, every corner of ours is compared with the nearest VI/49 point of the same code (of either kind: the two polar constellations' corners are flagged interpolated there, which is why 29 more corners are ours than original VI/49 corners). The chord drift is how far the shipped outline's straight lines lie from the same edges drawn at 0.02 degrees.

precession: IAU 1976 (Lieske) precession angles from B1875.0 (JD 2405889.25855) to J2000.0; no FK4 to FK5 equinox correction (about 0.07 arcseconds).
